title: Don't wrap already-focusable elements in Tooltip; it adds a second unlabeled tab stop
answers: Why does the drag handle have two tab stops, one with no accessible name?
Icon inside Tooltip creates an extra focusable element for screen readers
How to add hover text to an icon without breaking keyboard navigation
Tooltip component makes children focusable unexpectedly
body:
Symptom: a keyboard/screen-reader user tabs past a control (e.g. drag handle) and lands on an extra, unlabeled stop right after it.
Root cause: grafana-ui's Tooltip makes its child a tab stop by itself, so wrapping an Icon inside a Tooltip inside an already-focusable/aria-labeled container (e.g. a div with aria-label and dragHandleProps) creates a second, nameless stop — see public/app/features/notebook/scene/layout-notebook/edit/NotebookCellFrame.tsx:NotebookCellFrame.
Fix pattern: when the parent element is already focusable and labeled, drop the Tooltip wrapper and set the hover/accessible text via the Icon's title prop instead, reusing the same label string for both aria-label and title.
Constraints: applies when an icon sits inside an already-interactive, aria-labeled parent; for icons that are not otherwise focusable/labeled, Tooltip remains the right way to provide hover text.
applies: grafana-ui components combining Icon + Tooltip inside an already-focusable/aria-labeled parent

search: Do not wrap an Icon (or other element) in grafana-ui's Tooltip when the parent is already focusable and aria-labeled, as this creates a second, nameless keyboard tab stop. Instead, set hover text via the Icon's title prop, reusing the label string for both aria-label and title attributes. The rule applies to grafana-ui components where an Icon sits inside an interactive parent with aria-label. Tooltip wrapping remains appropriate for icons that are not otherwise focusable or labeled. Addresses accessibility issues in NotebookCellFrame and similar notebook scene components.
